TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Anterior translation of the tibia relative to the femur. Severe osseous stress response with impaction fracture along the sulcus terminalis of the lateral femoral condyle. Small osseous contusions along the posterolateral and posteromedial tibial plateau. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Moderate, partially ruptured Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: High-grade cartilage loss at the sulcus terminalis.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Completely ruptured and partially resorbed.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Grade 2 sprain.
Posterolateral corner structures: Mild edema in the posterolateral corner without ligamentous injury.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 13 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Soft tissue edema along the anteromedial joint line likely posttraumatic. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1. Complete rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament with pivot shift osseous contusions including an impaction fracture at the sulcus terminalis with severe osseous stress response.

2. Grade 2 sprain of the medial collateral ligament.

Findings:  Large knee joint effusion with a degree of synovitis. Large popliteal cyst measuring 3.3 cm x 2 cm x 5.6 cm. No sinister bone marrow changes.  Mild subcutaneous edema around the knee joint.  Intact cruciate and collateral ligaments.  Minor intrasubstance mucoid degeneration of the medial meniscus. No discrete tears. Degenerative tearing of the lateral meniscus on a background of mucoid degeneration, with partial extrusion of the body.  Normal appearance of the pes anserine tendons, popliteus tendon, distal biceps femoris tendon and distal iliotibial band.  Intact extensor mechanism.  Full-thickness chondral loss noted along the weightbearing portion of the lateral tibial condyle with underlying bone stress change. High-grade chondral thinning noted in the posterior weightbearing portion of the medial femoral condyle with minor underlying bone stress changes. Low-grade chondral thinning in the lateral tibiofemoral compartment, and the retropatellar facets. Lateral tibiofemoral and patellofemoral marginal osteophyte formation.  
Conclusion:  Large knee joint effusion with synovitis. Degenerative tearing of the lateral meniscus on a background of mucoid degeneration, with partial extrusion of the body. Marked lateral tibiofemoral osteochondropathy. Ancillary findings above.

FINDINGS:

Fluid:
Moderate knee joint effusion. Large popliteal cyst measuring 6.5 x 3.8 x 1.6 cm, with distal leakage suggesting rupture.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
Intrasubstance degeneration of the medial meniscus, with oblique tear of the body and posterior horn. Intact medial collateral ligament. Thinning of the medial femoral cartilage without full-thickness defect.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
Intrasubstance degeneration of the lateral meniscus, without tear. Intact lateral collateral ligament, iliotibial band and biceps femoris tendon. Preserved lateral femorotibial cartilage thickness without full-thickness defect.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
Intact anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
Mild tendinosis of the quadriceps and patellar tendons. Unremarkable Hoffa's fat pad. Cartilage fissuring of the lateral patellar facet, without full-thickness defect.

Bones:
Subchondral fracture of the medial femoral condyle without impaction and associated bone marrow edema.
Minimal bone marrow edema edema in the medial tibial plateau.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Normal.

CONCLUSION:

1. Large popliteal cyst, with distal rupture.

2. Oblique tear of the medial meniscus, involving the posterior horn and body.

3. Subchondral fracture of the medial femoral condyle, without impaction and associated bone marrow edema.

4. Medial compartment and patellar chondropathy, with mild superficial fissuring (grade 2).

5. Mild quadriceps and patellar tendinosis.
